All 6 backend tests pass. Both flows successful.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py confirm_payment: does not verify amount>0 before creating a subscription/marking booking paid. In mock mode a 0-XOF payment can still activate a subscription (Gratuit plan yields amount=0). Consider rejecting amount==0 or skipping is_premium activation for free-plan payments.

server.py confirm_payment: no idempotency lock — two concurrent confirm calls on the same payment_id could each pass the pending check and re-insert a subscription/notify twice. Consider using find_one_and_update({status:'pending'}) to atomically transition.

server.py initiate_payment for purpose='booking' does not check that booking price>0 or that booking is not already paid; a client could re-initiate on an already-paid booking. Add guard: if b.payment_status=='payé' -> 409.
PaymentDialog.jsx: phone validation `/^\d{9,}$/` allows arbitrarily long numeric strings; consider tighter Senegal format (e.g. 9 digits, starts with 7).
PaymentDialog.jsx: on success, dialog is closed BEFORE onSuccess() runs -> if refreshUser/load throws, the user has no visual signal. Consider awaiting the callback inside try/catch.
Subscription.jsx: 'Gratuit' plan (amount 0) also opens payment dialog; UX-wise a free plan should not go through Mobile Money — bypass PaymentDialog when p.price starts with 'Gratuit' or amount is 0.

Backend PAYMENTS_MODE is 'mock' and cron secret is committed in .env (WEBHOOK_CRON_SECRET). Fine for demo, but rotate before production and enforce PAYMENTS_MODE guard on confirm (reject 4-digit shortcut when mode != 'mock').
